steps.note: take the op from the Campaign Ops NPC named in the header

the page names no zone: "an area controlled in the Northern Area by the Beastman Confederate". Two ???s sit near the stronghold and the other one belongs to the Hawk Eye ops, so the page itself warns you to pick the correct one.

Touching the ??? sets up a bomb; it goes off after around 90 seconds. A beastman that wanders close disarms it (Notes bullet 1), which is why the wait belongs to this rung rather than being a rung of its own.

check the same ??? again after the explosion for "The stronghold has sustained considerable damage." Notes bullet 1: waiting too long after the explosion, Warping or leaving the area before this second click, or being K.O.'d all fail the op.
report back to finish the mission -- the op is not over at the ???

report back to complete the mission

notes:
Campaign Rank is a real gate with no schema field, so it is here and flagged rather than in gates.level, which means CHARACTER level: this op's rank is "Golden Star §§§§". gates.repeatable and gates.expansion are null because {{Campaign Header}} carries neither field and this page says nothing about either in words. Twelve bullets, six rungs. The Quartermaster's zone is NOT a guess and NOT inherited: the wikitext links [[Quartermaster - Bastok Markets (S)|Quartermaster]], so the page itself binds him to Bastok Markets (S), and the Bastok Markets (S) NPC list on BG Wiki confirms a Quartermaster at H-9. target.name is the plain in-game name "Quartermaster", not the wiki's disambiguated title, which would be a marker key nothing in game answers to. The hunt rung has no zone: the page says any Beastmen-controlled zone and explicitly that it need not be one of your own nation's, then lists fifteen zones across three beastman families. Exactly ONE Transporter has to die, but which family's depends on the zone you pick, so all three are recorded with count 1 and role kill and the OR is flagged; kill counts are display-only in this addon and never advance a step, so three candidates cost nothing and give the player a marker wherever they go. The two Guards are NOT recorded as mobs -- the page says they warp off on their own and never asks you to kill them. Bullets 5 and 7 sit slightly at odds (bullet 5 has the Transporter dying outright to any hit from behind under Sneak, bullet 7 gives it about 1500 HP and has you defeat it normally); both are kept in the note rather than one being picked. Bullets 6, 10 and 12 are advice and respawn timing, not rungs. The [KI] Beastman Confederate crate is honest evidence for the ??? rung: it is granted there, it is not in the Rewards field (which lists lower enemy Supplies, Experience Points and 900 Allied Notes), and it is then handed to the Quartermaster, so it appears as evidence exactly once and as a held item on the turn-in.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 3: All fifteen zone names already carry the (S) suffix on the page and all fifteen resolve.

steps.note: select Resource Procurement from the Campaign Ops menu

Hieronymus sends you to the Quartermaster at (H-9); the wikitext link target [[Quartermaster - Bastok Markets (S)]] is what puts him in Bastok Markets (S). He tells you to go to a "Beastman influenced" area, attack any Beastmen Supply Divisions and seize their cargo.

Any Beastmen-controlled zone, and the page says it need not be one in your allied nation's area, so no zone is recorded. Kill ONE Transporter Quadav in Crawler's Nest (S), Grauberg (S), North Gustaberg (S), Pashhow Marshlands (S), Rolanberry Fields (S); Orcish in Batallia Downs (S), East Ronfaure (S), Jugner Forest (S), The Eldieme Necropolis (S), Vunkerl Inlet (S); Yagudo in Fort Karugo-Narugo (S), Garlaige Citadel (S), Meriphataud Mountains (S), Sauromugue Champaign (S), West Sarutabaruta (S). A Sneak Attack, critical hit, or any hit from behind under Sneak kills it outright (bullet 5); bullet 7 instead gives it about 1500 HP and has the two Guards warp off shortly after, which is why the Guards are not recorded as kills.

click the ??? where the Transporter died for the [KI] Beastman Confederate crate. It disappears after a couple of minutes; you get it even if you did not help kill the Transporter, and you cannot get it at all if you are not on the op.

return with the crate and speak to the Quartermaster at (H-9). Bullet 10 notes you do NOT have to see him again before obtaining the key item, which is why this rung sits after the ??? and not before it.
report back to Hieronymus to complete the mission -- the op does not end at the Quartermaster

Three bullets, three rungs, all three targets named. The Adjutant's grid (J-9) is on this page twice -- in the walkthrough and in the header Description -- but his ZONE is not, so Bastok Markets (S) comes from the Bastok Markets (S) NPC list on BG Wiki, which places an Adjutant at J-9; the Adjutant NPC page itself has only the San d'Oria entry filled in. The three earlier Bastok tiers (Iron Anvil I (B), II (B), III (B)) give the same (J-9) with the same giver, which is corroboration, not the source. The five sub-bullets under bullet 2 are all conditions on that one conversation, not rungs: a developed craft at level 61 or he turns you away, a timed menu, TWO recipes, failure for slowness or wrong picks, and up to eight ingredients with a "No more ingredients are required" option. That level 61 is a CRAFT level, so gates.level stays null -- putting it there would gate the op on character level, which the header gives as Any. The "Recipes" section after the walkthrough is an unfilled placeholder table whose rows literally read "Item name / Ingredients", with a single real Clothcraft row (Aketon); it is reference material and contributes no steps.

steps.note: talk to Hieronymus and select this Campaign Op

the Adjutant asks which craft you specialize in, then tests you on TWO recipes from it: crystal first, then up to eight ingredients, with a time limit on each selection and failure for a wrong or late pick. Requires a developed craft at level 61 or better -- a craft level, not a character level. Grid (J-9) is from this page; the zone is from the Bastok Markets (S) NPC list on BG Wiki.
once both tests are done, go back to Hieronymus for the reward
